resources.string: Sum of connector, adapter and other connection losses at the operating frequency. Enter 0 to exclude them. Do not count losses already included in a measured assembly twice.
Enter a value from 0 to 1000 dB.
With zero attenuation, this model does not limit length. This is an idealization, not a valid length for a real cable.
Connection losses exceed the specified limit. No cable length satisfies it.
Connection losses use up the allowed loss. Only a zero cable length satisfies it.
Length is rounded down to a centimetre; lengths below a centimetre are shown in millimetres. Loss and power use the displayed length.
The scale shows the fraction of input power at the line output, including the specified connection losses.

Estimate for a matched line using attenuation at the selected frequency. The user specifies the allowed loss. Only the entered connection losses are included. Mismatch, temperature changes, cable power rating and communication range are not calculated.

Aallowed — the total allowed line loss specified by the user, in dB.

Aconnections — the total connector, adapter and other connection losses at the same operating frequency, in dB.

α — attenuation of the specific cable model over reference length L₀ at the operating frequency, in dB/100 m or dB/100 ft.

L₀ — reference length: 100 m or 30.48 m (100 ft). Lmax — physical cable length in metres. Velocity factor does not enter this formula.

When Aconnections exceeds Aallowed, no length satisfies the limit. When they are equal and α is positive, only zero length satisfies it. At α = 0, this model gives no finite length limit.
Line loss versus physical cable length. %1$s.
The length limit depends on the allowed loss and cable attenuation.
Calculate the maximum physical cable length from the allowed loss.

Acable = α × L / L₀
Aline = Acable + Aconnections
T = 10⁽⁻ᴬline/¹⁰⁾
P₂ = P₁ × T
ΔP = P₁ × (1 − T)
Acable is the cable loss; Aline is the total cable and specified connection loss, in dB. T is the output power fraction; P₁ and P₂ are input and output power; ΔP is the power lost in the line.

Example: Aallowed = 3 dB, Aconnections = 0.4 dB, α = 6.3 dB/100 m. This leaves 2.6 dB for the cable; the maximum length rounded down is 41.26 m. The 3 dB limit is an example, not a recommendation. Do not count connectors already included in a measured assembly again in Aconnections.
